[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

> **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.

25	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
26	
27	The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
28	
29	Install the skill:
30	
31	```bash filename="Terminal"
32	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
33	```
34

36

38	Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
39	```

41	## Or adopt by hand
42	
43	To adopt an existing app by hand:
44	
45	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
46	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
47	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
48	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
49	5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.
50	
51	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
52	
53	## Enable Partial Prefetching
54	
55	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
56	
57	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
58	
59	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
60	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
61	
62	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
63	  cacheComponents: true,
64	  partialPrefetching: true,
65	}
66	
67	export default nextConfig
68	```
69	
70	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
71	
72	## What changes for `<Link>`
73	
74	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
75	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
76	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
78	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
79	
80	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
81	
82	## Migrate existing full prefetches
83	
84	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
85	
86	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
87	
88	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
89	
90	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
91	
92	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same assertions after adopting the destination. A failure identifies UI the App Shell no longer carries, so you can cache the data or subtree that restores it. The passing test provides regression coverage.

102	<Link href="/about">About</Link>
103	```

245	### URL data
246	
247	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
248	
249	### Real-time content
250	
251	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
252	
253	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
254	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
255	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
256	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
257	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
258	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
259	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

568	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
569	
570	## What "instant" means
571	
572	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
573	
574	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
575	
576	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
577	
578	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
579	
580	<details>
581	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
582	
583	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
584	
585	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
586	
587	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
588	
589	</details>
590	
591	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.

627	## The tools
628	
629	### Build the static shell
630	
631	With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell.
632	
633	> **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the Optimizing prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching.
634	
635	**`<Suspense>`** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves.
636	
637	> **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `<Suspense>` boundary further up the tree is needed. For a link with `prefetch={true}`, [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) makes URL data available before navigation, so the fallback can become part of the prefetched UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback.
638	
639	Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route, which renders during client navigations while remaining content streams. Partial Prefetching uses the App Shell as the default `<Link>` prefetch. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached content that depends on that link's URL data.
640	
641	### Prefetch URL data for a link
642	
643	Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `<Link>` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. Links to the same route share one App Shell instead of triggering a separate App Shell request for each link.
644	
645	To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch):
646	
647	```tsx
648	<Link href="/checkout" prefetch>
649	  Checkout
650	</Link>
651	```
652	
653	With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click.
654	
655	### Validate instant navigation
656	
657	By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `<Suspense>` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached.
658	
659	To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`:
660	
661	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7}
662	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
663	
664	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
665	  cacheComponents: true,
666	  experimental: {
667	    instantInsights: {
668	      validationLevel: 'manual-warning',
669	    },
670	  },
671	}
672	
673	export default nextConfig
674	```
675	
676	<details>
677	<summary>How validation simulates different navigations</summary>
678	
679	For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy.
680	
681	For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks:
682	
683	- **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `<Suspense>` catches everything.
684	- **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation.
685	
686	Each case is validated independently. A `<Suspense>` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows.
687	
688	</details>

690	### Test it in CI
691	
692	The `@next/playwright` package provides an [`instant()`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#testing-instant-navigation) helper that scopes your assertions to the UI that's immediately available on navigation, so regressions surface in CI. 702	## A page that navigates instantly
703	
704	To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The goal is that navigating to and between products is instant.

706	The product page fetches two pieces of data: product details (name, price) and live inventory.
707	
708	- There is no `generateStaticParams`, meaning `slug` is only known at request time
709	- Both components await `params` to get the `slug`, which suspends. Each has its own `<Suspense>` boundary
710	- **Product info** rarely changes and is queried from the db using a cached function
711	- **Inventory** must be fresh on each request. The db query is inside a `<Suspense>` boundary

718	  return (

720	      <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading product...</p>}>
721	        <ProductInfo params={props.params} />
722	      </Suspense>
723	      <Suspense fallback={<p>Checking availability...</p>}>
724	        <Inventory params={props.params} />
725	      </Suspense>
726	    </div>

728	}

730	type Params = PageProps<'/store/[slug]'>['params']

732	async function ProductInfo({ params }: { params: Params }) {
733	  const { slug } = await params
734	  const product = await getProduct(slug)

744	  'use cache'
745	  return db.products.findBySlug(slug)

862	## Prevent regressions with e2e tests
863	
864	Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship.
865	
866	The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Install it alongside `@playwright/test`:
867	
868	```bash package="pnpm"
869	pnpm add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
870	```
871	
872	```bash package="npm"
873	npm install -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
874	```
875	
876	```bash package="yarn"
877	yarn add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
878	```
879	
880	```bash package="bun"
881	bun add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test
882	```
883	
884	A route can be reached two ways, and a `<Suspense>` boundary can cover one without covering the other:
885	
886	- **Initial page load**: Use `page.goto()` to test the static UI from the document response.
887	- **Client navigation**: Click a `<Link>` to test the destination's prefetched UI. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) can add request-specific content to this UI.
888	
889	```typescript filename="e2e/navigation.test.ts" highlight={6-14,20-25}
890	import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'
891	import { instant } from '@next/playwright'
892	
893	test.describe('Product page (/store/[slug])', () => {
894	  test('is instant on an initial page load', async ({ page, baseURL }) => {
895	    await instant(
896	      page,
897	      async () => {
898	        await page.goto('/store/hats')
899	        await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap')
900	        await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0)
901	      },
902	      { baseURL }
903	    )
904	    await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible()
905	  })
906	
907	  test('is instant on a client navigation', async ({ page }) => {
908	    await page.goto('/store/shoes')
909	    await instant(page, async () => {
910	      await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]')
911	      await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/store/hats')
912	      await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap')
913	      await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0)
914	    })
915	    await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible()
916	  })
917	})

920	Pass Playwright's `baseURL` to `instant()` when `page.goto()` is the first navigation. The helper needs the origin before requesting the document.
921	
922	Inside the callback, an initial page load shows the static UI and a client navigation shows the destination's prefetched UI. Other dynamic content remains blocked until the callback finishes.

926	For client navigations, wait for the destination URL before asserting on its UI. Otherwise, a shared selector can match the source page before the destination commits. If the prefetched destination cannot commit, the URL wait times out and the test fails.

943	## Fixing a navigation that blocks
944	
945	Consider a different route, `/products/[slug]`, that fetches product data from a public API and shows a featured list alongside:
946	
947	```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx"
948	export default async function ProductPage(
949	  props: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>
950	) {
951	  const featured = await getFeatured()
952	  const { slug } = await props.params
953	  const res = await fetch(`https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/products/${slug}`)
954	  const product = await res.json()
955	
956	  return (
957	    <div>
958	      <FeaturedSection items={featured} />
959	      <h1>{product.name}</h1>
960	      <p>${product.price}</p>
961	      <p>{product.description}</p>
962	    </div>
963	  )
964	}
965	
966	async function getFeatured() {
967	  const res = await fetch('https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/products?limit=3')
968	  return res.json()

973

1067	### Iterate on loading states
1068	
1069	{/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */}
1070	
1071	Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `<Suspense>` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation.
1072	
1073	The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. A product page that keeps the header, image, and description visible with only the price and availability behind a fallback feels faster than a full-page skeleton, even at the same total load time.
1074	
1075	Use the [DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) to see what your users see, or see the [AI workflow](#ai-workflow) for automating the loop with an agent.
1076	
1077	## AI workflow
1078	
1079	At a high level, an agent optimizes a single navigation like this:
1080	
1081	- **Observe**: read validation insights and choose the exact navigation and UI that should appear immediately.
1082	- **Test**: confirm the target UI renders normally, then write an `instant()` test and verify that it fails before changing the route.
1083	- **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or `<Suspense>`). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation.
1084	- **Verify**: run the test against a production-like build and keep the passing test as a regression guard.
1085	
1086	The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model, only to follow the insights and errors until they're gone. It does need your app-specific intent, though. Tell it what should appear immediately, what can stream in, and what must stay fresh. When a caching decision is unclear, keep the data fresh behind `<Suspense>` rather than guessing a cache lifetime.
1087	
1088	For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down.
1089	
1090	Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers:
1091	
1092	- **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell.
1093	- **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile.
1094	- **Per-link prefetching** (nav-only): when a route reads URL data (`searchParams` or `params`), opt it into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) so the framework resolves that data at link-prefetch time. Session data from `cookies()` or `headers()` already lands in the App Shell without it.
1095	
1096	Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect.
1097	
1098	For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). With React DevTools enabled it reports the component tree and which `<Suspense>` boundaries are still pending, so an agent can make a change, snapshot the shell, check what landed, and adjust. See [Runtime visibility](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility) in the AI agents guide for the setup.
1099	
1100	The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill packages this loop. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both.
1101	
1102	## Opting out
1103	
1104	Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes.
1105	
1106	The dev overlay surfaces this as the **Block** fix alongside every insight:
1107	
1108	<FixCardGrid>
1109	  <FixCard
1110	    group="block"
1111	    title="Allow blocking route"
1112	    href="/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic#allow-blocking-route"
1113	    snippets={[
1114	      { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
1115	      { text: 'export const instant = false', highlight: true },
1116	    ]}
1117	  />
1118	</FixCardGrid>
1119	
1120	Set `instant = false` on the page or layout file. This opts the segment out of validation feedback. The segment may still navigate instantly if its structure supports it; the framework just won't surface insights for it. Navigations between sibling segments below are still validated.
1121	
1122	```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx"
1123	export const instant = false
1124	```
1125	
1126	With `false` on `/dashboard/layout.tsx`, validation no longer flags navigations into `/dashboard` from outside; navigations between `/dashboard/a` and `/dashboard/b` are still checked.
1127	
1128	For opted-out segments, the navigation blocks on the server. If the content depends on cookies or headers but has a known cache lifetime, caching it with [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) lets the App Shell carry it ahead of the click instead of opting out, as long as its [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time is at least 5 minutes.

41	## Or adopt by hand
42	
43	To adopt an existing app by hand:
44	
45	1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
46	2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
47	3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
48	4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
49	5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.
50	
51	Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
52	
53	## Enable Partial Prefetching
54	
55	> **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
56	
57	Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
58	
59	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
60	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
61	
62	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
63	  cacheComponents: true,
64	  partialPrefetching: true,
65	}
66	
67	export default nextConfig
68	```
69	
70	After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
71	
72	## What changes for `<Link>`
73	
74	| `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
75	| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
76	| `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
77	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
78	| `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
79	
80	The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
81	
82	## Migrate existing full prefetches
83	
84	Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
85	
86	A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
87	
88	> **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
89	
90	### Verify prefetched UI with tests
91	
92	To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same assertions after adopting the destination. A failure identifies UI the App Shell no longer carries, so you can cache the data or subtree that restores it. The passing test provides regression coverage.

245	### URL data
246	
247	[URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
248	
249	### Real-time content
250	
251	A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
252	
253	| Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
254	| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
255	| [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
256	| [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
257	| [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
258	| [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
259	| [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |

568	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
569	
570	## What "instant" means
571	
572	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
573	
574	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
575	
576	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
577	
578	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
579	
580	<details>
581	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
582	
583	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
584	
585	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
586	
587	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
588	
589	</details>
590	
591	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.

627	## The tools
628	
629	### Build the static shell
630	
631	With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell.
632	
633	> **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the Optimizing prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching.
634	
635	**`<Suspense>`** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves.
636	
637	> **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `<Suspense>` boundary further up the tree is needed. For a link with `prefetch={true}`, [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) makes URL data available before navigation, so the fallback can become part of the prefetched UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback.
638	
639	Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route, which renders during client navigations while remaining content streams. Partial Prefetching uses the App Shell as the default `<Link>` prefetch. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached content that depends on that link's URL data.
640	
641	### Prefetch URL data for a link
642	
643	Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `<Link>` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. Links to the same route share one App Shell instead of triggering a separate App Shell request for each link.
644	
645	To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch):
646	
647	```tsx
648	<Link href="/checkout" prefetch>
649	  Checkout
650	</Link>
651	```
652	
653	With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click.
654	
655	### Validate instant navigation
656	
657	By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `<Suspense>` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached.
658	
659	To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`:
660	
661	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7}
662	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
663	
664	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
665	  cacheComponents: true,
666	  experimental: {
667	    instantInsights: {
668	      validationLevel: 'manual-warning',
669	    },
670	  },
671	}
672	
673	export default nextConfig
674	```
675	
676	<details>
677	<summary>How validation simulates different navigations</summary>
678	
679	For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy.
680	
681	For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks:
682	
683	- **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `<Suspense>` catches everything.
684	- **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation.
685	
686	Each case is validated independently. A `<Suspense>` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows.
687	
688	</details>

1068	
1069	{/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */}

1071	Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `<Suspense>` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation.

1103	
1104	Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes.

events.content:
Done. The dashboard links now prefetch just the project title, and the rest of the project page renders only when the user actually navigates. I verified this against a production build by requesting the same URL with the router's prefetch headers versus its navigation headers: the prefetch payload for `/projects/acme` contains "Acme Storefront" and the details fallback but none of the description or activity items, while the navigation payload contains everything.

**What changed**

This Next.js version has a "Partial Prefetching" model where a route renders in three stages: a shared App Shell (no URL-dependent content), an optional per-link prefetch that resolves `params` for links with `prefetch={true}`, and the navigation itself. The change places the title in stage two and the details in stage three:

- `next.config.ts` — enabled `partialPrefetching: true` (it requires `cacheComponents`, which was already on).
- `app/page.tsx` — added `prefetch={true}` to the project links. Under Partial Prefetching this opts the link into a per-link prefetch that resolves the slug and any cached content behind it, rather than the legacy "fetch the whole page" behavior.
- `app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` — split the single `Project` component into two Suspense-wrapped children. `ProjectTitle` awaits `params` and the cached `getProjectTitle`, so the per-link prefetch resolves it. `ProjectDetails` awaits `unstable_navigation()` before reading anything, which keeps that subtree out of both the App Shell and the per-link prefetch; the user sees "Loading details..." briefly while it streams in after the click. `getProjectDetails` stays `use cache`, so it keeps its cache lifetime on the navigation.

Two things worth knowing:

- The `Promise.all` that previously fetched title and details together is gone; that was the reason the title couldn't appear early (both were tied to the same Suspense boundary and the 800ms details delay).
- `next build` rewrote `tsconfig.json` on its own (`jsx` to `react-jsx`, an added `.next/dev/types` include, and reformatting). It reported the `jsx` change as mandatory, and it would reapply these on any `next dev`/`next build`, so I left them. It also generated `next-env.d.ts`, `.next/`, and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` as untracked files.

`unstable_navigation()` is marked experimental (added in 16.4.0), so its name may change in a future release.
